title: Wire Private observability minimum pack (dashboards + alerts) into Helm values
author: Diego Santos
description: This PR wires the v1 "Private observability minimum pack" artifacts (Grafana dashboard bundle + Prometheus alert/recording rules) into the `redwood-private` Helm chart values, with customer-friendly toggles and sane defaults. Motivation: today Private installs often require manual copying of dashboards/rules, which makes upgrades brittle (e.g., empty dashboards after upgrade) and makes it harder for Support/SRE to assume a baseline. This change makes the minimum pack installable via `values.yaml` and version-pins the artifact bundle so air-gapped installs can package it reliably. What’s included: (1) Dashboards: ships a versioned dashboard bundle as ConfigMaps that work with the Grafana sidecar pattern. Customers can enable/disable per-category (runtime, control-plane, infra) and choose the label/key used by their Grafana sidecar. (2) Alerts/recording rules: ships `PrometheusRule` resources when the Prometheus Operator CRD is present; otherwise can optionally emit rules as a raw rules ConfigMap for non-operator Prometheus setups. (3) Exporter + retention toggles: adds values to enable/disable the recommended minimum exporters (kube-state-metrics, node-exporter, DCGM exporter) when customers choose to deploy the bundled stack, and exposes retention / storage knobs for Prometheus (and Grafana persistence when enabled). Non-goals: this does not introduce "premium" features (federation, long retention defaults, custom dashboards). It also does not force-install Prometheus/Grafana; by default we only ship artifacts and create ServiceMonitors/PrometheusRules when enabled. Values summary (new): `observability.enabled` (default true), `observability.dashboards.enabled` (default true), `observability.dashboards.sidecar.label` (default `grafana_dashboard`), `observability.dashboards.sidecar.folderAnnotation` (default `grafana_folder`), `observability.alerts.enabled` (default true), `observability.alerts.mode` = `prometheusOperator|configMap` (default `prometheusOperator`), `observability.alerts.runbookBaseUrl` (used to stamp alert annotations), `observability.stack.enabled` (default false; if true installs `kube-prometheus-stack` + exporters with bounded defaults), `observability.stack.prometheus.retention` (default `15d`), `observability.stack.prometheus.storage.size` (default `50Gi`), `observability.stack.exporters.kubeStateMetrics.enabled` (default true when stack enabled), `observability.stack.exporters.nodeExporter.enabled` (default true when stack enabled), `observability.stack.exporters.dcgmExporter.enabled` (default true when stack enabled). Implementation notes: dashboards and rules are imported from the `observability-pack` bundle (pinned by version in chart values) and rendered into templates via a small helper that keeps ConfigMaps under the Kubernetes size limits by splitting across multiple ConfigMaps. PrometheusRule creation is gated on both values and CRD presence (`monitoring.coreos.com/v1`). Alert annotations include: summary, description, severity, and `runbook_url` pointing to our internal runbooks (base URL configurable for customer docs mirrors in air-gapped environments). Testing: `helm template` on defaults; `ct lint` for chart schema; kind-based smoke deploy with Grafana sidecar and Prometheus Operator verifying dashboards appear and Prometheus loads rules. Related: ENG-19152 (chart wiring), PRs in `observability-pack` adding the bundles, and installer preflight work in `redwood-private-installer` (separate PR) to validate CRDs/storage prerequisites.
commits: redwood-private: add observability values schema + docs comments
templates: render dashboard bundle into labeled ConfigMaps (split by size)
templates: add PrometheusRule resources + CRD gating + configMap fallback
charts: optional kube-prometheus-stack wiring behind observability.stack.enabled
alerts: stamp runbook_url annotations from configurable base URL
ci: add chart-testing job to validate new values permutations
conversation: Dylan Brooks (review): Can we avoid assuming a specific Grafana sidecar label? Some customers use `grafana_dashboard` but others use `grafana_dashboard: "1"` patterns. Author (Diego): Added `observability.dashboards.sidecar.label` and `observability.dashboards.sidecar.labelValue` (default empty -> just key exists), plus `folderAnnotation` override; updated README comments. Logan Wright (review): PrometheusRule should be gated on CRD presence; we’ve seen installs without operator. Also we need a safe fallback. Author: Added `.Capabilities.APIVersions.Has "monitoring.coreos.com/v1"` gating; introduced `alerts.mode=configMap` that emits a rules ConfigMap (customer can mount into Prometheus) and documented it. Allison Grant (review): Please ensure alert severities map to our Private standards and include runbook URLs. Also recording rules should be separate so they can be disabled if cardinality is an issue. Author: Updated annotations to include `runbook_url` and clarified severity mapping in values comments; added `observability.recordingRules.enabled` toggle (default true) and grouped recording rules into a separate manifest section. Rafael Mendes (review): Default retention/storage for bundled Prometheus feels too low for some clusters and too high for others; can we document sizing guidance and keep defaults conservative? Author: Kept defaults at 15d/50Gi but added explicit values and comments; linked to infra sizing doc in README; also set CPU/mem requests for kube-prometheus-stack components behind the stack flag only. Chloe Martin (review): ConfigMaps can exceed size limits with dashboard JSON. How are we splitting? Author: Added helper to split by dashboard file and chunk by byte limit; validated template output < 900KiB per ConfigMap; added a chart-testing install job with stack enabled + dashboards enabled. Final: Approvals from Dylan, Logan, Allison; Rafael approved after re-run; merged via squash.
release_notes: Private Helm chart now supports installing the minimum supported observability artifacts (Grafana dashboards + Prometheus alerts/recording rules) via values toggles.
Optional bundled Prometheus/Grafana stack can be enabled behind `observability.stack.enabled`, with configurable retention/storage and exporter toggles.
Alert resources include configurable runbook URLs to support customer doc mirrors in air-gapped environments.
